title: Descriptive Text
summary: In-depth exploration of descriptive genres: identification and description schemes, sensory language, adjectival phrases, spatial organization, and inferring the author's tone.

lessons.title: Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description

blocks.html:
Communicative Purpose and Generic Structure of Descriptive Text

The primary social function of a Descriptive Text is to describe a specific person, place, historical landmark, or natural object by painting a vivid mental image in the reader's mind.

Unlike an informational report (which discusses general classes of things, like 'Lions in Africa'), a descriptive text focuses on a singular, specific entity (e.g., 'Borobudur Temple', 'The Grand Canyon', or 'My Siamese Cat Luna').

blocks.title: Real-World Context: How Architecture Catalogs and Travel Journals Paint with Words
blocks.html: When National Geographic introduces a newly discovered ancient citadel or a biological research paper describes a rare orchid species, they do not tell a fictional story. They construct a Descriptive Text: capturing the physical appearance, unique features, habitat, and distinctive qualities of a specific entity so vividly that readers can picture it clearly in their minds.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: John Swales and Communicative Genre Analysis
blocks.html:
Tokoh: John Swales Tahun: 1990 M Krisis: Learners confuse descriptive writing with narrative storytelling, producing rambling chronological diaries instead of structured spatial depictions of a subject.

Linguist John Swales published Genre Analysis: English in Academic and Research Settings (1990). Swales established that text genres are defined by their social communicative purpose and follow distinct obligatory rhetorical stages recognized by discourse communities worldwide.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: The Generic Structure of Descriptive Texts
blocks.html: A Descriptive Text aims to describe a particular person, place, or thing in vivid detail. Generic Structure: 1. Identification: Introduces and identifies the specific phenomenon or subject to be described. 2. Description: Systematically elaborates on parts, physical qualities, characteristics, functions, or behavioral habits of the subject.

blocks.title: Key Language Features of Descriptive English Texts
blocks.html:
Focus on Specific Participant → Simple Present Tense → Attributive & Identifying Verbs → Rich Adjective Phrases
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Focus on Specific ParticipantFocuses on ONE unique entity (e.g., 'The Raja Ampat Archipelago', not islands in general)Singular specificity
Simple Present TenseUses timeless present tense to state enduring physical characteristics and factsGrammatical stability
Attributive & Identifying VerbsDominant use of relational processes ('is', 'has', 'features', 'consists of')State of being
Rich Adjective PhrasesEmploy sensory descriptors: 'crystalline turquoise waters', 'majestic limestone karsts'Vivid imagery

Pedagogical Note: In reading tests: The opening paragraph almost always serves as the Identification stage.

blocks.title: Simulasi Interaktif: Dekonstruksi Struktur Teks Deskriptif
blocks.caption: Petakan bagian kalimat wacana ke dalam blok Identifikasi atau Deskripsi Detail secara visual.

blocks.title: Pembeda Utama: Report vs Descriptive
blocks.html: Jika teks membahas 'Volcanoes' secara umum (pembentukan tektonik, tipe-tipe magma), itu adalah Report Text. Jika teks mendeskripsikan 'Mount Bromo' secara spesifik (lokasi di Jawa Timur, lautan pasir berbisik, tangga menuju kawah), itu adalah Descriptive Text.

blocks.title: Applied Analytical Scenario: Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description
blocks.question: How can a critical reader analyze and verify discourse arguments regarding 'Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description' based on principles articulated by John Swales?

steps.step: Identify Textual Claims and Operational Constraints
steps.explanation: Examine the core assertions in the target text and locate the explicit warrants connecting premises to the central thesis of Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description.

steps.step: Evaluate Evidence Quality and Rhetorical Framing
steps.explanation: Cross-examine whether the supporting data meets scholarly standards, checking for potential logical fallacies or biases.

steps.step: Synthesize Authorial Stance and Strategic Implications
steps.explanation: Determine the underlying communicative purpose and synthesize actionable conclusions aligned with John Swales's framework.

blocks.answer: By systematically evaluating textual evidence and logical structure, readers can resolve complex comprehension challenges regarding Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description with critical confidence.

blocks.title: Comprehension Check: Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description
blocks.question: Which of the following statements most accurately reflects the core principle established by John Swales regarding 'Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description'?

options.A: The concept relies entirely on subjective guesswork without requiring any textual or empirical justification.
options.B: The principle provides a rigorous analytical framework grounded in verifiable evidence and coherent logical relations.
options.C: The rule is completely obsolete and has been universally rejected by all modern academic institutions.
options.D: The structure can only be applied when reading ancient fictional poetry and is invalid for academic prose.
options.E: The framework mandates that readers must accept all internet claims without checking author credibility.

blocks.explanation: Option B is correct. In academic discourse, Text Anatomy: General Identification and Detailed Description establishes systematic criteria for rigorous critical analysis. Option A is incorrect because validity requires evidence. Option C is false as the framework remains foundational. Option D is incorrect because it applies across academic genres. Option E contradicts the principles of critical evaluation.
blocks.hint: Identify the option emphasizing evidence-based reasoning, logical consistency, and scholarly integrity.

lessons.title: Sensory Details, Imagery, and Spatial Adverbials

blocks.html:
Evoking the Senses: Sensory Imagery in Descriptive Prose

Skilled authors do not merely state facts; they evoke human senses through sensory language. Recognizing sensory descriptors helps you interpret inferential questions about setting and atmosphere.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Engaging the Reader's Five Senses
blocks.html: Compare these two sentences: 1. 'The bakery was good.' 2. 'The warm scent of toasted cinnamon and melting butter drifted through the frosted glass door, accompanied by the gentle clatter of porcelain coffee cups.' The second sentence uses Sensory Details: pulling your sense of smell, sight, and hearing into an immersive mental world.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Lakoff & Johnson and Embodied Cognition
blocks.html:
Tokoh: George Lakoff & Mark Johnson Tahun: 1980 M Krisis: Descriptions read like dry telephone directories ('the room is big and white'), failing to stimulate the reader's sensory imagination.

Cognitive linguists George Lakoff and Mark Johnson in Metaphors We Live By (1980) demonstrated that human abstract thought is grounded directly in bodily sensory experiences (sight, sound, physical orientation, temperature, and touch).

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Sensory Modalities and Spatial Cohesion
blocks.html: Sensory Details appeal to human sensory receptors: Visual (color, shape, light), Auditory (echoes, rustling, humming), Tactile (coarse, velvety, freezing), Olfactory (pungent, fragrant), and Gustatory (savory, bittersweet). Spatial Adverbials (e.g., adjacent to, towering above, nestled within) guide the reader's eye through a logical physical layout.

blocks.title: Spatial Progression Patterns in Descriptive Writing
blocks.html:
Top-to-Bottom → Outside-to-Inside → Near-to-Far (Perspective)
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Top-to-BottomFrom the snow-capped peak of the mountain down to the emerald pine valley belowVertical panning
Outside-to-InsideFrom the weathered stone facade entering into the sunlit central courtyardArchitectural entrance
Near-to-Far (Perspective)From the pebbles at one's feet extending outward to the hazy ocean horizonDepth of field

Pedagogical Note: Look for spatial prepositions to track the author's physical vantage point in descriptive reading comprehension.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Citraan Indrawi
blocks.question: Excerpt: 'As visitors step into the ancient courtyard, the air grows noticeably damp and cool. Towering granite pillars, heavily carpeted with emerald moss, rise toward a vaulted ceiling where morning sunlight filters through narrow stone embrasures.' Which senses are engaged?
steps: Indera Peraba (Tactile): 'damp and cool' (kelembapan dan kesejukan udara).
Indera Penglihatan (Visual): 'emerald moss' (lumut hijau zamrud), 'towering granite pillars', 'morning sunlight filters through narrow stone embrasures'.
Tata Letak Spasial: 'step into the courtyard', 'rise toward a vaulted ceiling'.
blocks.answer: Teks memadukan citraan perabaan suhu udara dan penglihatan arsitektural untuk menciptakan suasana sakral dan kuno.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Which phrase from a descriptive text utilizes TACTILE imagery?

options.A: The deafening roar of the waterfall echoed across the gorge.
options.B: Coarse, sun-baked sand scratched against their bare feet.
options.C: Gleaming crimson banners hung from the palace balcony.
options.D: A pungent aroma of roasted spices permeated the kitchen.

blocks.hint: Tactile berkaitan dengan sentuhan atau tekstur kulit.
blocks.explanation: 'Coarse, sun-baked sand scratched against their bare feet' melibatkan sensasi rabaan kasar dan panas pada kulit (tactile).

lessons.title: Language Features: Simple Present Tense, Modifiers, and Participles

blocks.html:
Grammatical Hallmarks of Descriptive Text

To portray enduring qualities and timeless characteristics, descriptive texts rely on a rigorous set of syntactic structures:

  • Simple Present Tense: Expressing permanent states, factual attributes, and inherent geographic properties (e.g., 'The island spans over 500 square kilometers...').
  • Relational and Action Verbs: Verbs of being/possession (consist of, feature, overlook, stand, encompass) and action verbs depicting motion within the space.
  • Complex Noun Phrases: Packing dense sensory data using ordered pre-modifiers (adjectives) and post-modifiers (prepositional and participial phrases).

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Why We Say 'A Big Red Apple' but Never 'A Red Big Apple'
blocks.html: English descriptive grammar has strict unspoken rules that give writing its vivid texture. Native speakers instinctively know the precise ordering of multiple adjectives and the subtle difference between an 'exciting journey' (-ing participle modifying the noun) and an 'excited traveler' (-ed participle reflecting internal feeling).

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Randolph Quirk and Comprehensive English Grammar
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Randolph Quirk Tahun: 1985 M Krisis: Students write or interpret descriptive sentences with scrambled adjective orders and confused participial modifiers.

Linguist Sir Randolph Quirk and his colleagues published A Comprehensive Grammar of the English Language (1985). Quirk formalized the universal order of attributive adjectives and the syntactic role of sensory adverbials in descriptive registers.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Key Grammatical Features of Descriptive Text
blocks.html: Descriptive texts rely primarily on the Simple Present Tense (for timeless physical attributes), Attributive Adjective Chains (following the OSASCOMP order), and Relational Processes (linking verbs such as is, look, appear, feel).

blocks.title: Descriptive Grammatical Syntax Blueprint
blocks.html:
Subject (Entity) → Relational / Sensory Verb → Attributive Adjective Stack (OSASCOMP) → Spatial / Locative Adverbial
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
OSASCOMP OrderOpinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose'A magnificent (O) huge (S) ancient (A) circular (Sh) grey (C) Greek (Or) marble (M) temple (P)'
Present Participial (-ing)Active modifier describing the entity causing the sensation'The breathtaking view...', 'The towering mountain...'
Past Participial (-ed)Passive modifier describing the internal state or condition'The abandoned village...', 'The exhausted climbers...'
Spatial AdverbialsPrepositional phrases anchoring the entity in space'Nestled between two ridges...', 'Perched atop a limestone cliff...'

Pedagogical Note: Descriptive reading passages test your ability to trace how spatial adverbials guide the reader's visual imagination from foreground to background.

blocks.title: Contoh Penguraian Frasa Partisipial
blocks.question: Sentence: 'Perched atop the jagged limestone cliffs, the sanctuary overlooks the tempestuous ocean.' What does 'Perched' modify?
steps: Step 1: Identifikasi bentuk kata kerja: 'Perched atop...' adalah past participial phrase.
Step 2: Temukan subjek utama setelah tanda koma: 'the sanctuary' (tempat suci / kuil).
Step 3: Terjemahkan relasi gramatikal: Sanctuary itulah yang bertengger (perched) di puncak tebing kapur terjal.
Step 4: Fungsi kalimat: Memberikan orientasi lokasi dramatis sebelum klausa utama 'overlooks the tempestuous ocean'.
blocks.answer: 'Perched' memodifikasi 'the sanctuary', menjelaskan posisi letak geografisnya yang berada di puncak tebing.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Choose the correct adjective order to complete the descriptive sentence: 'The temple is renowned for its ________ bell.'
blocks.explanation: Urutan OSASCOMP yang tepat: Size (massive) mendahului Age/History (historic) dan Material (bronze).

lessons.title: Inferring Atmosphere, Mood, and Author's Perspective

blocks.html:
Tone vs Mood: Reading the Emotional Resonance of a Place

TKA questions frequently probe beyond literal facts to ask: 'What is the tone of the author?' or 'What mood does the passage evoke?'

  • Tone: The author's personal attitude toward the subject matter (e.g., reverent, admiring, objective, nostalgic, critical). Detected through word connotations and rhetorical questions.
  • Mood / Atmosphere: The emotional atmosphere felt by the reader (e.g., serene, eerie, majestic, somber, uplifting). Created through sensory imagery and pacing.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Two Descriptions of the Same Haunted Manor
blocks.html: Consider two descriptions of an old mansion: One calls it 'a venerable historical landmark steeped in romantic nostalgia'. The other calls it 'a rotting, decaying carcass choked with menacing shadows'. The physical bricks are identical, but the atmosphere (mood) and authorial tone are polar opposites.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: I.A. Richards and Practical Criticism
blocks.html:
Tokoh: I.A. Richards Tahun: 1929 M Krisis: Test-takers focus exclusively on factual objects mentioned in a description, completely missing the emotional atmosphere and authorial mood.

Literary scholar I.A. Richards published Practical Criticism (1929). Richards established that text interpretation involves four distinct planes of meaning: Sense (plain facts), Feeling (author's emotional attitude), Tone (author's stance toward the reader), and Intention (communicative goal).

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Tone vs Mood / Atmosphere in Literature
blocks.html:
Tone: The author's attitude toward the subject matter, conveyed through diction and syntactic choices (e.g., reverent, skeptical, melancholy, satirical).

Mood (Atmosphere): The prevailing emotional environment created for the reader (e.g., somber, eerie, tranquil, whimsical).

blocks.title: Tone and Atmosphere Decoding Matrix
blocks.html:
Examine Sensory Adjectives → Audit Lexical Connotations (+ / - / neutral) → Identify Rhetorical Figures (Metaphors/Similes) → Deduce Author's Underlying Tone
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Reverent / Awe-Inspired'Sublime, majestic, pristine, towering, timeless splendor'Describing natural wonders or heroic architecture.
Somber / Melancholy'Bleak, desolate, rotting, silent, forgotten, gray, withered'Describing ruins, autumn landscapes, or post-war scenes.
Critical / Disdainful'Pretentious, gaudy, sterile, overcrowded, ostentatious'Describing commercial tourist traps or poorly designed spaces.
Objective / Informative'Comprising, measuring, constructed from, situated at'Neutral encyclopedic travel guides or scientific accounts.

Pedagogical Note: When an exam question asks 'The author's attitude toward the monument is...', eliminate extreme options that contradict the passage's connotative vocabulary.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Nada Penulis
blocks.question: Excerpt: 'Standing beneath the towering arches of the cathedral, one cannot help but be humbled by the sheer ambition of medieval stonemasons who dedicated lifetimes to erect monuments that touch the heavens.' What is the author's tone?
steps: Diksi kunci: 'humbled' (merasa rendah hati di hadapan keagungan), 'sheer ambition' (ambisi luar biasa), 'touch the heavens' (menyentuh langit).
Sikap penulis: Memuji dedikasi dan pencapaian monumental para perajin batu masa lampau.
Klasifikasi nada: Nada kagum dan penuh rasa hormat (admiring, reverent, awestruck).
blocks.answer: Nada penulis adalah reverent / full of admiration (penuh kekaguman dan penghormatan).

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: An author describes an abandoned castle as: 'crumbling ramparts consumed by wild brambles, where lonely winds mourn among forgotten halls.' What atmosphere is created?
blocks.hint: Perhatikan kata 'crumbling', 'lonely winds mourn', dan 'forgotten halls'.
blocks.explanation: Diksi kehancuran dan kesunyian menciptakan atmosfer muram dan terlantar (melancholic and desolate).

lessons.title: Evaluating Objectivity: Factual Characteristics vs Subjective Impressions

blocks.html:
Fact vs Subjective Impression in Travelogues and Guides

Descriptive texts in the TKA frequently blend verified physical facts with promotional rhetoric or subjective travel reflections. Critical literacy requires you to separate what can be empirically proven from what represents the author's personal impression.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Travel Brochures vs Honest Travelers' Reviews
blocks.html: A luxury resort advertisement describes their beach as 'paradise on earth with heavenly tranquil waters'. A travel journalist reports: 'The beach spans 300 meters of white coral sand with average water temperatures of 28°C and moderate surf breaks'. Learning to separate verifiable descriptive reports from subjective aesthetic judgments is critical for critical literacy.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: S.I. Hayakawa on Language in Thought and Action
blocks.html:
Tokoh: S.I. Hayakawa Tahun: 1949 M Krisis: Readers treat subjective promotional exaggerations in travel brochures as verifiable objective facts.

Semantics pioneer S.I. Hayakawa authored Language in Thought and Action (1949). Hayakawa categorized all human utterances into three distinct tiers: Reports (verifiable by third-party observation), Inferences (statements about the unknown based on the known), and Judgments (expressions of personal approval or disapproval).

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Objective Descriptive Report vs Subjective Aesthetic Judgment
blocks.html:
Objective Report: A verifiable statement that describes physical attributes without emotional coloring or subjective value claims.

Aesthetic Judgment: A statement reflecting an observer's personal taste, emotional response, or subjective evaluation of beauty.

blocks.title: Descriptive Claim Classification Matrix
blocks.html:
Analyze Descriptive Clause → Can It Be Measured or Photographed Objectively? → Is It a Value Judgment? → Classify: Verifiable Report vs Subjective Impression
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Verifiable Physical Report'The pagoda stands 67 meters tall, supported by 12 solid teakwood columns.'Directly verifiable by measurement or photographic evidence.
Aesthetic Evaluation'It is the most breathtaking sanctuary ever constructed by human hands.'Unverifiable subjective opinion; reflects author's admiration.
Sensory Description'The pungent aroma of roasting cloves drifted through the narrow alley.'Grounded in physical senses, though individual perception varies.
Distractor TrapTest asks for 'A factual characteristic of the building'Beware options quoting the author's glowing subjective superlatives.

Pedagogical Note: In TKA questions asking for factual details, always select options supported by empirical data rather than emotive praise.

blocks.title: Contoh Membedakan Fakta dan Opini
blocks.question: Text: '(1) Lake Toba is the largest volcanic lake in the world, occupying a caldera formed by a supervolcanic eruption 74,000 years ago. (2) Samosir Island sits gracefully in the lake's center. (3) The tranquil waters provide an unparalleled sanctuary that completely relieves all urban exhaustion.' Which sentence is an opinion?
steps: Kalimat (1): Fakta ilmiah terverifikasi (danau vulkanik terbesar, erupsi 74.000 tahun lalu).
Kalimat (2): Fakta geografis (pulau Samosir di tengah danau) dengan adverbial deskriptif 'gracefully'.
Kalimat (3): Opini subjektif ('unparalleled sanctuary', 'completely relieves all urban exhaustion' adalah klaim hiperbolis personal yang tidak dapat diukur secara seragam pada setiap orang).
blocks.answer: Kalimat (3) merupakan opini / impresi subjektif penulis.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Which of the following statements represents a verifiable FACT rather than an opinion?

options.A: The canyon offers the most serene sunset experience on the continent.
options.B: The national park covers an expanse of approximately 1,200 square kilometers.
options.C: Visitors will undoubtedly find the steep trail delightfully charming.
options.D: No other museum in the world displays artifacts of comparable grandeur.

blocks.hint: Fakta dapat diverifikasi dengan pengukuran angka dan batas wilayah.
blocks.explanation: Luas wilayah 1.200 kilometer persegi adalah ukuran terverifikasi secara matematis dan geografis (fakta), sedangkan pilihan lain memuat opini subjektif ('most serene', 'delightfully charming', 'no other museum comparable').

lessons.title: Common Pitfalls: Confusing General Categories with Specific Subjects

blocks.html:
Anatomy of Distractors in Descriptive Reading Items

TKA test developers engineer plausible wrong answers by exploiting cognitive shortcuts. When answering questions on descriptive texts, guard against the following three recurring pitfalls:

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Tigers in General vs 'My Pet Tiger Shera'
blocks.html: If an encyclopedia entry discusses 'The Siberian Tiger (Panthera tigris altaica): habitat, diet, and hunting behaviors', is it a descriptive text? No! In English genre pedagogy, that is an Information Report because it describes an entire biological class. A true Descriptive Text describes one specific, tangible subject, such as 'The Royal Bengal Tiger Rescued at Way Kambas Sanctuary'.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: S.I. Hayakawa and the Ladder of Abstraction
blocks.html:
Tokoh: S.I. Hayakawa Tahun: 1939 M Krisis: Students confuse a 'Report Text' (which describes classes of things in general) with a 'Descriptive Text' (which describes one specific unique thing).

Semanticist S.I. Hayakawa introduced the famous Ladder of Abstraction in Language in Action (1939). Hayakawa showed that confusion arises when speakers jump between high abstraction levels (general species/concepts) and low abstraction levels (specific unique objects).

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Report Text (General) vs Descriptive Text (Specific)
blocks.html: Report Text: Describes the way things are in general as a representative class of natural or synthetic phenomena (e.g., 'Whales are marine mammals...'). Descriptive Text: Describes a particular, individualized subject (e.g., 'The Blue Whale Specimen at London Natural History Museum'). Recognizing this boundary prevents selecting generic distractors.

blocks.title: Diagnostic Checklist: Report vs Descriptive
blocks.html:
Subject Specificity → Communicative Purpose → Introductory Stage
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Subject SpecificityReport: Plural general nouns ('Smartphones', 'Volcanoes') | Descriptive: Proper noun or definite singular ('Mount Bromo', 'The iPhone 15 Pro')Core contrast
Communicative PurposeReport: Classifying and documenting scientific facts | Descriptive: Depicting a particular individual entityRhetorical goal
Introductory StageReport: General Classification | Descriptive: IdentificationStructural signature

Pedagogical Note: If the text discusses a category of animals or phenomena as a whole using plural nouns, classify it as a Report Text.

blocks.title: Tiga Jebakan Utama Soal Descriptive Text
blocks.html:
1. The Overgeneralization Trap: Memilih opsi yang menggeneralisasi seluruh spesies atau fenomena dunia, padahal teks hanya mendeskripsikan satu subjek tunggal tertentu.
  2. The Spatial Inversion Trap: Memutarbalikkan tata letak ruang (misalnya: menyebut patung berada di dalam gua, padahal teks menyatakan patung berdiri di pelataran luar menghadap mulut gua).
  3. The True-Detail Misattribution: Mengaitkan karakteristik objek A ke objek B yang sama-sama disebutkan dalam paragraf yang sama.

blocks.title: Contoh Identifikasi Jebakan Distraktor
blocks.question: Question: 'What is the primary focus of the passage?' Options: (A) The geological evolution of volcanic calderas across Indonesia. (B) The architectural layout and landscape features of Mount Kelud's crater lake. (C) The socio-economic lives of villagers living near active volcanoes.
steps: Analisis Teks: Teks mendeskripsikan kawah Gunung Kelud, suhu air danau kawah, kubah lava baru, dan jalur pendakian menuju puncak.
Evaluasi (A): Overgeneralization trap! Teks hanya membahas Kelud, bukan seluruh gunung berapi di Indonesia.
Evaluasi (C): False focus trap! Penduduk desa hanya disebut sepintas sebagai pemandu wisata.
Evaluasi (B): Benar! Menangkap fokus spesifik subjek yang dideskripsikan.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: In a text specifically describing 'The Sydney Opera House', a distractor claims: 'Modern performing arts centers globally require acoustic sail-shaped shells.' What makes this distractor invalid?

options.B: It overgeneralizes a unique feature of one building to all performance centers globally.
options.C: It contradicts the architectural history of Australia.
options.D: It uses archaic vocabulary not understood by high school students.

blocks.explanation: Distraktor tersebut melakukan generalisasi berlebih (overgeneralization) dari satu bangunan unik menjadi kebutuhan seluruh gedung pertunjukan di dunia.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Descriptive Text Practice and Quiz

blocks.html:
Mastery Checklist: Descriptive Text

Before launching into the official chapter quiz, verify that you can comfortably:

  • Differentiate the general identification opening from subsequent detailed feature descriptions.
  • Trace spatial adverbials to construct an accurate mental layout of the subject.
  • Analyze sensory diction and infer the author's tone toward the described subject.
  • Eliminate overgeneralized distractors and distinguish objective facts from travel impressions.

blocks.title: Simulasi Mandiri
blocks.html: Kerjakan kuis 20 butir soal berikut dengan konsentrasi penuh. Perhatikan rujukan pronomina dan sinonim frasa deskriptif.

blocks.title: Cheat Sheet: Descriptive Text Genre Architecture
blocks.subtitle: Summary of social function, generic structure (Identification & Description), sensory adjectives, and author's purpose.
blocks.html:
1. Generic Structure

  • Identification: Introduces and identifies the specific phenomenon, place, animal, or person to be described.
  • Description: Describes parts, qualities, physical characteristics, behavior, and unique features in vivid detail.

2. Linguistic Features

  • Specific Participant: Focuses on one specific entity (e.g., "The Borobudur Temple", not temples in general).
  • Simple Present Tense: Predominantly uses verbs of condition and state (is, has, stands, overlooks).
  • Sensory Imagery: Rich adjectives describing color, size, texture, sound, and atmosphere.

blocks.text: Kuis Uji Kompetensi TKA Bahasa Inggris: Descriptive Text (20 Soal Pilihan Ganda Terstandar).
